### Observed differences

- In the later window, A25 is followed by A28 in about 98% of its outgoing transitions, whereas before it was followed by A36, A37, A42 and A43 (each about 20–27%) and never by A28. [DIR001, LAG001]
- A28 is no longer a successor of A36, A37, A42 or A43: before it received about 20–27% of their outgoing transitions, after it receives about 1% or less. Instead, A31 now receives about 20–26% of those transitions, where before it received none. [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024]
- A26 now branches to A37, A43, A42 and A36 (each about 10–17% of its transitions) and to A27 in about 48%, whereas before it went to A27 in about 99%. When A26 co-occurs with A36, A37, A42 or A43, it now usually precedes them, whereas before they preceded A26. [DIR002, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- A27, A36, A37, A42 and A43 each appear in about half of traces in the later window, down from all traces; their mean occurrences per trace drop from about 1.0 to about 0.5. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- A27 and the group A36/A37/A42/A43 now almost never co-occur (about 1–2% of traces), whereas before they co-occurred in all traces. A28 and A31 also often occur without A27 in the later window. [REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016]
- Positionally, A28 moves earlier (mean position from about 0.47 to 0.39 of the trace), while A36, A37, A42 and A43 move later (from about 0.40 to about 0.58). A25 and A28 become adjacent (lag 1 in about 98% of co-occurring cases, previously lag 5). [POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in routing: A25 now leads to A28, A28 is no longer a successor of the A36/A37/A42/A43 group, A31 takes over that successor role, and A26 now routes to that group with a reversed order, while participation of A27 and the A36/A37/A42/A43 group is roughly halved. The consistency across occurrence, direction, relation, position and lag indicators points to a coordinated reorganisation rather than isolated fluctuations. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, LAG001]

A competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out is that the later window reflects a different case mix or a new variant that replaces the old one, rather than a modification of a single stable process. However, the large and mutually consistent changes in routing, order and participation make a structural change the most plausible interpretation. Some lag items are based on very few observations in the later window, but the main directional and relational evidence rests on hundreds of traces. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011, LAG012]
